newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan oil monopoly to continue Vietnam project.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan oil monopoly to continue Vietnam project.

text.p: Taiwan's state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Thursday it would continue a refinery investment in Vietnam despite its decision to freeze overseas investment.
"Our Vietnam refinery project will continue as it is already on our 1995/96 (July/June) budget approved by parliament," a company spokesman said by telephone.
Chinese Petroleum said on Thursday it would halt new overseas investments temporarily in response to the economics ministry's call to strengthen local investments.
Chinese Petroleum has said it and another Taiwan firm would take 10 percent of the US$1.6 billion Vietnam refinery project. Other partners include Vietnam, South Korean, U.S. and Malaysian oil firms.
The spokesman said the oil monopoly also would continue its US$11 million liquefied petroleum gas project in Vietnam, but halt a US$16 million solvent project there.
All overseas investment projects still in the initial contact phase, including those in Latin America, would be halted temporarily, he said.
The company also would freeze projects that are listed on the firm's stalled 1996/97 (July/June) budget, which has yet to be approved by parliament, executives said.
"Once parliament passes the budget, we will immediately continue those investments, but the investments may be hurt because of the delay," spokeswoman Ho Li-chun said.
Contracted projects would continue as planned.
"We will continue all the overseas projects that we have already signed contracts with," Ho said.
Many of the contracted projects were included in the previous year's budget and have parliamentary approval.
Among the projects being halted are a petrochemical zone development project in Malaysia and an oil refinery in Brunei, Ho said.
All planned projects in Indonesia will be halted, the spokesmen said, including a proposal to move CPC's mothballed No. 2 naphtha cracker there.
